speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: This is important because our Parliament is where laws are passed and the country’s future is charted.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Looking around the world, we can find many examples of parliaments, or equivalent legislatures, degenerating into dysfunction.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Many of them are of older and purportedly exemplary democracies that the rest of the world should aspire towards.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Proceedings at many of these legislatures or parliaments sometimes look like "reality TV".

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Legislators or parliamentarians shout, interrupt, fight or do whatever they can to prevent a genuine debate.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: What is more concerning is the amount of half-truth rhetoric that can be promulgated inside and outside of the parliaments.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Some of these ideas even garnered enough support from their people to change the course of their country, often for the worse.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: The parliament is a reflection of the society, but it also sets the tone for the society.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: A dysfunctional parliament tends to go hand-in-hand with a society that is highly cynical and distrusting of their politicians and public institutions.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: There is a small number of people who are cynical of everything and extreme in the way they see the world.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: However, the vast majority of our people are reasonable, rational and still exhibit a high level of trust.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: This majority is precious, they are the ones who will decide on the fate of the country.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: We need to be careful with the kind of ideas we promulgate.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: We may unwittingly cause fissures, as well as erode trust and cohesion in our society.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Having rigorous debates on policies and issues in the parliament is important.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: Bringing up alternative viewpoints is critical to preventing us from groupthink.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: However, there is a constructive way to do it.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao (Nominated Member)
text: I hope our parliamentarians can be an inspiration for Singaporeans on how to engage with each other on difficult subjects.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Nominated Member for his very pertinent speech, which was both thoughtful and incisive.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It serves as a timely reminder of the importance of an effective Parliament in service of the nation and an opportunity to reflect on what being an effective Parliament really means.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Parliament is where the Government is held to account, where issues of national importance are debated and matters of public interest are explained.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is where our laws are made and also where the direction of the country is set and the future of our people is determined, through the Bills and the Motions that Members of Parliament vote on.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Parliament is also the place where our national identity and the character and soul of our society, is shaped through the values we espouse, words we say and the decisions we make.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Thus, what we say and do in Parliament has a profound impact on the lives of Singaporeans and the future of Singapore.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is a privilege that must be exercised responsibly and in the best interest of our people and our country.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have seen what has happened in other countries, where their Parliaments are gridlocked, hamstrung or so hopelessly at loggerheads that the country cannot move forward.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is their people who pay the price.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Certainly, there must be robust debate, so that policies and recommendations can be scrutinised and assumptions tested.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But the quality and integrity of the debate also matters greatly.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Mr Cheng suggested four principles to guide how issues should be brought up and debated.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I agree with these and would add one more.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But let me first address the four principles he raised.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is important because decisions are made and opinions are influenced based on our deliberations.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That is why Members are expected to be able to substantiate any statements made by them, if challenged.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But beyond factual accuracy is the deeper underlying principle of honesty and integrity, because people must be able to trust what we say.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: While some things are straightforward, a good deal of the issues confronting Singapore today are manifold and complex.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Oversimplifying them does not give our people a true picture.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Given our small size and limited resources, there are always trade-offs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Advocating a position, without at the same time highlighting relevant downsides, does our people a disservice.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Advancing generous policies, without telling people how they will be paid for or where the money to pay for it ultimately comes from, creates false hopes which will ultimately end in disappointment.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Seeking easy options, such as using up the reserves without good justification rather than creating sustainable revenue streams, undercuts our resilience and chips away at fundamental principles of prudence and responsibility.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It is par for the course that matters brought before the House should be vigorously debated, questioned and scrutinised.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: However, at the end of the day, irrespective of our political stripes, we must have the same overriding objective, which is to improve the lives of Singaporeans and help Singapore prosper.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have seen the effect of this in other Parliaments and the outcomes are not pretty.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Those were scenes we never expected to see in America, the bastion of democracy.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But they happened and they happened as a result of deep polarisation.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But what we must avoid in our Parliament is the politics of division.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: There is a difference between reflecting genuine ground concerns, which is our duty and the deliberate stoking of anger and creating or intensifying of divides, which is not only wrong, but dangerous.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As Members of Parliament, we not only have to reflect the concerns of the people and give voice to the aspirations of Singaporeans, but also exercise our judgement on issues and speak up for what we believe in, even if it is contrary to the prevailing or most popular view, to persuade our fellow Members and the public at large as to what is the best solution to a difficult problem, or what is the most important issue before the country.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Parliament's deliberations should shape the public discourse and set the direction for the country.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have to think not only about the here and now, but also for the future.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We must think not only for one group, but for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Singapore is unique and special and we have come this far because our Parliaments before us did what was right for us.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That task is now ours and we must discharge it to the best of our abilities.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Cheng, would you like to withdraw your amendment.

speaker: Mr Cheng Hsing Yao
text: Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Is the hon Member given leave to withdraw his amendment?
